title: Representativeness as a Forgotten Lesson for Multilingual and Code-switched Data Collection and Preparation

bias_targets.methodology: Training Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models on a code-switched dataset from one location (Hong Kong) and evaluating them on a dataset from another location (Singapore) to measure the cross-regional performance gap (MER and CER), alongside a systematic survey of location metadata across 68 datasets.

Conducting a meta-analysis of 68 code-switched speech and social media datasets to quantify the percentage that document and represent diverse age, gender, and language proficiency backgrounds for both the data generators (speakers/users) and the data preparers (collectors/transcribers/annotators).

Analyzing 68 surveyed datasets to measure the overrepresentation of English-centric language pairs and the overrepresentation of informal registers (e.g., social media and conversational data) at the expense of other languages and formal code-switching contexts.
